title: Quantifying and Improving the Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Language Models Against Spurious Features in Grounding Data
research_problem: RALMs frequently latch onto spurious features or superficial lexical overlap in retrieved grounding data rather than genuine supportive facts.
proposed_method: SURE framework: diagnostic quantification of spurious grounding correlation and robustness regularization.
dataset: Open-domain QA (Natural Questions, TriviaQA) and Synthetic Perturbations
metrics: Exact Match, Token F1, Spurious Attribution Rate
main_findings: Models degrade significantly when distractors contain superficial lexical shortcuts. Robustness tuning mitigates shortcut reliance.
limitations: Evaluates large closed/open LLMs requiring high GPU VRAM. Benchmark datasets differ from standard SQuAD.
code_availability: Code promised in camera-ready; Needs verification from full paper
compute_notes: Requires 24-48GB VRAM for full replication; student adaptation needs compact lightweight models.
robustrag_extension: Direct inspiration for RobustRAG's hard distractor selection and cross-encoder mitigation test.
reading_notes: Candidate Anchor Paper. Highly relevant formulation of grounding noise and spurious lexical competition.

title: The Distracting Effect: Understanding Irrelevant Passages in RAG
research_problem: Investigates how irrelevant passages in the retrieved context window degrade generation accuracy and cause hallucinations.
proposed_method: Systematic controlled distractor injection analysis across varying noise positions and context depths.
main_findings: Answer quality drops sharply even when a single irrelevant passage is introduced; position of distractor influences error rate.
limitations: Focuses primarily on large LLMs; does not extensively benchmark cross-encoder rerankers on compact edge setups.
compute_notes: Moderate compute (can run via API or single GPU).
robustrag_extension: Motivates RobustRAG's Experiment A (noise quantity curve) and Experiment C (relevance reranking).
reading_notes: Strongest conceptual alignment with our research question. Proves context noise causes severe degradation.

title: RAGGED: Towards Informed Design of Scalable and Stable RAG Systems
research_problem: Trade-offs between retriever latency, candidate document pool size, and downstream generation stability.
proposed_method: Empirical benchmarking framework assessing stability boundaries across dense, sparse, and hybrid retrieval.
main_findings: Expanding retrieval pool k increases recall but introduces severe context clutter that destabilizes downstream QA.
limitations: Complex multi-component pipeline; high infrastructure overhead.
compute_notes: Heavy compute requirements for multi-dataset BEIR sweeps.
robustrag_extension: Provides theoretical rationale for RobustRAG's Experiment D (top-k filtering ablation).
reading_notes: Validates that larger context windows are not inherently better; filtering is necessary.

title: InfoGain-RAG: Boosting Retrieval-Augmented Generation through Document Information Gain-based Reranking and Filtering
research_problem: Standard semantic similarity rerankers often select redundant or noisy passages that do not maximize factual gain.
proposed_method: Information-gain objective that penalizes redundant information and ranks complementary supportive evidence.
metrics: Multi-hop F1, Information Entropy, Token F1
main_findings: Information-gain reranking outperforms standard cross-encoders on complex multi-hop queries.
limitations: High scoring latency per document pair; requires multi-step entropy calculation.
compute_notes: Moderate compute; feasible for student extension.
robustrag_extension: Informs our reranker analysis by showing the boundary where standard cross-encoders fail on noisy pools.
reading_notes: Demonstrates that reranking ordering directly determines generation success.

title: Astute RAG: Overcoming Imperfect Retrieval Augmentation and Knowledge Conflicts for Large Language Models
research_problem: How language models resolve knowledge conflicts when retrieved passages contradict internal parametric knowledge or other passages.
proposed_method: Iterative evidence consensus weighting and conflict-aware generation prompting.
main_findings: Models are highly susceptible to misleading conflicting context, often abandoning valid internal knowledge.
limitations: Does not evaluate small compact models (e.g. FLAN-T5) or lexical BM25 hard distractors.
compute_notes: High API cost if replicated with GPT-4.
robustrag_extension: Highlights the vulnerability of generators to deceptive surface evidence, motivating our failure analysis.
reading_notes: Key paper for discussing why distractors succeed in misleading the reader model.
